## Overview

**mhpfilter** splits macroeconomic time series into a trend and a cycle with the Hodrick-Prescott (HP) filter and
two versions whose settings come from the data:

* `hp_filter()`: the HP filter with a fixed smoothing parameter (1600 quarterly, 100 annual);
* `mhp_filter()`: the modified HP filter of McDermott (1997), assessed by Choudhary, Hanif and Iqbal (2014): every
  series gets the smoothing parameter that minimises a generalised cross-validation criterion (the published
  approximation, or the exact criterion);
* `fmhp_filter()`: the fully modified HP filter of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017), which also reduces the
  end-point bias of the HP filter by raising the smoothing parameter at the first and last observations, with
  linear or quadratic weights chosen to minimise the end-point loss of Bloechl (2014).

Around them:

* many series at once (`mhp_batch()`, `fmhp_batch()`), the filters compared (`mhp_compare()`, `batch_compare()`,
  `fmhp_compare()`);
* the weights, gain functions and end-point loss of any HP-type filter (`hp_weights()`, `hp_gain()`, `hp_loss()`,
  `hp_schedule()`);
* simulated trend-plus-cycle series and the power comparison of the papers (`mhp_designs()`, `mhp_simulate()`,
  `fmhp_simulation()`);
* `ggplot2` graphics, a plain-language interpretation of every result (`mhp_interpret()`), the references of every
  method (`mhp_cite()`) and an application that runs all of this without code (`mhp_app()`).

Version 1.0.0 keeps every function, argument and result of version 0.1.0 and adds the fully modified HP filter.
Every filter is one banded linear solve, so the search over 100000 values of the smoothing parameter for 200 observations
takes 1.3 s instead of 6.4 s, and longer series gain more; the fully modified HP filter reproduces the published MATLAB code, and the end-point
losses of the HP filter in Tables 3a and 3b of Hanif et al. (2017) are reproduced.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("mhpfilter")
# development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/mhpfilter")
```

## Quick start

```{r quick}
library(mhpfilter)
data(us_macro)
gdp <- ts(data = us_macro$gdp, start = c(1959, 1), frequency = 4)
fm <-
  fmhp_filter(
      x               = gdp
    , max_lambda      = 3000
    , k_linear        = 15
    , k_quadratic     = NULL
    , alpha_linear    = seq(from = 0, to = 2000, by = 10)
    , alpha_quadratic = seq(from = 0, to = 2000, by = 5)
    , schemes         = c("linear", "quadratic")
    , form            = "rows"
    , lambda          = NULL
    , log_scale       = TRUE
    , as_dt           = FALSE
    )
fm
fmhp_compare(
    x          = gdp
  , frequency  = "quarterly"
  , max_lambda = 3000
  , log_scale  = TRUE
  , end_share  = 0.1
  )
```

```{r quick-plot, fig.height = 6}
plot(x = fm)
```

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
print(citation(package = "mhpfilter")[1L], style = "text")
```

BibTeX:


references of a single result.
